_README: Kit-blessed TanStack versions and the provenance of our vendored reference docs.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS: TanStack publishes no LTS. There is no `lts` dist-tag on any
TanStack package and no support-window policy — only a single rolling line per
library. So there is no upstream stability signal to defer to, and THIS FILE IS THE
LTS: the kit blesses one version per package and every project runs it. One project
upgrades = all projects upgrade, decided here, not per repo.
EXACT VERSIONS, NOT RANGES. A caret range lets a fresh install drift to a version
the kit never blessed, which defeats lockstep silently. Consumers declare these
versions exactly in package.json; scripts/check-tanstack.mjs fails on a range.
ENFORCEMENT is scripts/check-tanstack.mjs — CI job `tanstack-standard` plus
commit.sh pre-commit. That script is deliberately HERMETIC: it reads package.json
files, this manifest and sync-substitutions.json, and never touches the network.
The `watch` block below is for the maintainer review command, which does have
network and is run by hand.
CHANGING A VERSION is a maintainer act, via the kit's /review-tanstack command.
Do not bump a version here to make a project's build pass.

_packages_notes.@tanstack/react-table: v9.0.0, GA 2026-08-04 after 54 alphas + 80 betas. v8 is NOT the conservative alternative — its last release was 8.21.3 on 2025-04-14. Do not use legacyCreateColumnHelper: open upstream TS issue (aggregationFn rejects built-in string identifiers).
_packages_notes.@tanstack/react-router-ssr-query: Glue package. Sole export setupRouterSsrQueryIntegration({router, queryClient}) — wires QueryClientProvider plus SSR dehydrate/hydrate/streaming. Required wherever Query is used with Start.
_packages_notes.@tanstack/react-form-start: Start integration for Form: formOptions, createServerValidate, getFormData, mergeForm. Versioned in lockstep with react-form.

banned.react-hook-form: Use @tanstack/react-form. NOTE: `npx shadcn add form` installs this as a hard dependency — do not use shadcn's form atom; build field components against TanStack Form instead.

_form_rule: Form-library adoption is decided PER APP, all-in within an app. Three states,
and the third is a hard failure:
1. app declares @tanstack/react-form           -> decided, nothing to record
2. app listed in FORM_LIB_EXEMPT_APPS          -> deliberately decided no
3. app in neither                              -> question never asked, FAIL
FORM_LIB_EXEMPT_APPS is a space-separated app-name list in
.claude/sync-substitutions.json, read at runtime (same shape as DEPLOY_WORKFLOWS).
Exempt suits apps with no real data entry — ecommerce/cart surfaces, marketing
pages, and control-plane/service apps whose UI is a couple of status screens.
Data-entry apps (ERP browses and record forms) take the library.

references_rejected.*/migrate-*: Migrations are one-offs. Carrying a migration guide forever is exactly the stale-content problem the kit exists to avoid. SKILL.md tells a session where to read one from node_modules when it actually needs it. Covers migrate-from-nextjs, migrate-from-react-router, migrate-v8-to-v9.
references_rejected.@tanstack/react-start :: react-start: The upstream Start index skill — a table of contents pointing at its sub-skills. Our SKILL.md IS our index; carrying a second one just splits navigation.
references_rejected.@tanstack/react-start :: react-start/ser: We do not use React Server Components. Revisit if that changes — it is a substantial skill with 6 worked examples and would be worth vendoring then.
references_rejected.@tanstack/react-table :: with-tanstack-v: No @tanstack/react-virtual in the blessed set yet. Vendor when virtualised lists are adopted, not before.
references_rejected.@tanstack/react-table :: create-table-ho: Covered by table-getting-started.md for our usage. Revisit if we start building shared table hooks.

_references_rejected_notes: Upstream skills we have consciously decided NOT to carry, with the reason.
This block exists so /review-tanstack can tell 'decided against' apart from
'nobody has looked at this yet'. Without it every review re-surfaces the same
candidates as undecided, and a genuinely new upstream skill gets lost in the
repeat noise — the same three-state problem FORM_LIB_EXEMPT_APPS solves for
_link_rewrites_notes: Upstream skills link to each other by their nested paths. Vendoring flattens
them into one folder, so those links must be rewritten or they dangle.
This map is the SINGLE SOURCE for that transform, used in BOTH directions:
re-vendoring applies it to the upstream file, and the drift check applies it
to the upstream copy before diffing. Without the second use, every rewritten
link reports as drift on every review — permanent noise that would train the
maintainer to ignore a real hand-edit.
router-query maps to ../SKILL.md because react-router does not publish that
composition skill; our bible owns Router+Query.
_references_notes: Vendored from the SKILL.md files TanStack ships inside its npm packages, into
WHY VENDOR RATHER THAN READ node_modules: node_modules is not a skill source for
any agent tool, and the shipped files are NOT regenerated per release — every
router/start skill declares library_version 1.166.2 while riding inside packages at
1.168-1.171. So 'always current with the installed version' is not on offer, and
the auto-currency argument for pointing at node_modules buys nothing.
DELIBERATELY NOT VENDORED: every migrate-* skill (migrate-from-nextjs,
migrate-from-react-router, migrate-v8-to-v9). A migration is a one-off; carrying
its guide forever is the stale-content problem. The bible's discovery section says
where to read them in the session that needs one.
NO UPSTREAM SKILL EXISTS for TanStack Query or TanStack Form — verified: zero
SKILL.md files in query-core, react-query, form-core, react-form, and no skills/
directory anywhere in the TanStack/query or TanStack/form repos. Our Query and Form
guidance is hand-written in the bible and is the only content here with no upstream
